question: Should OpenClaw add a native ASR/STT backend seam for voice input, and if so should the first supported slice be macOS batch Push-to-Talk, broader Talk/Wake flows, or plugin-only provider work?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the safe product shape spans native capture UX, provider/config ownership, credential forwarding, private-network trust, fallback behavior, and batch-versus-streaming semantics.

options.title: Approve macOS batch PTT first
options.body: Add a small backend boundary for finished Push-to-Talk recordings, route transcription through a gateway/provider path with Apple Speech still default, and leave wake/realtime/webchat follow-ups separate.

options.title: Keep as broad design tracker
options.body: Leave this issue open until maintainers choose a cross-platform ASR model that covers PTT, Talk, Wake, and webchat together.

options.title: Plugin-only for now
options.body: Do not add native ASR settings yet; direct custom providers to ClawHub/plugin work and open a core issue only if a concrete missing SDK seam is proven.

recommendation.title: Approve macOS batch PTT first
recommendation.body: Add a small backend boundary for finished Push-to-Talk recordings, route transcription through a gateway/provider path with Apple Speech still default, and leave wake/realtime/webchat follow-ups separate.

likelyOwner.reason: The first unresolved product choice is in the native macOS voice-input boundary that Peter introduced and has most heavily maintained.
